about: The old sync engine's parity corpus (#813, for the replay in #814): every named scenario of the pre-merge Effortless plugin's `src/sync/computeSync.test.ts`, as the two notes before and the old plugin's own output after.

Recorded, not retyped. The old suite was run at the commit below with its test harness swapped for a recorder that captured each `describe` block's one `computeSync` call (input and output) and each assertion it executed, with its line and message. 245 assertions ran and all 245 passed, the same count the old suite prints for itself. The recorder is not in this repository, because it wraps the old test file.

Lines are the note's text split on `\n`. An `after` of null means the old plugin returned that note unchanged. Every scenario ran with `settings`: the collection is named `My Project`, today is 2026-03-25.

`direction` is the old plugin's only notion of which side changed: it ran `from-project` when the person left the collection and `from-daglogg` when they left today's log, and each direction ran different steps. This plugin has no direction, so `editedSide` records the side each scenario's own premise, read from its comments, says the person edited; `neither` means the scenario expects nothing to happen, and `unstated` means its comments do not say.

The old pairing comment is `%% eid:<id> %%`; this plugin's is `%% task-consistency:<eid> <hash> %%`. The texts carry the old form. An old assertion that looks for `%% eid:` reads as: the line carries the pairing marker for that eid. An id written `NEW-1`, `NEW-2`, ... is one the old plugin generated during that scenario (at random: `Date.now()` in base 36 plus four random characters), numbered in order of first appearance in the output, collection first, and replaced so the file does not change from one recording to the next.

`namedDifferences` carries each row of #709 § Named differences whose answer the old output does not bind. Row 2 marks every scenario whose old output holds a line rebuilt from parts — a copy into the log, a text or date sync, a line filed from the log, or a subtask re-indented on its way to the completed heading — so the replay compares fields there, not bytes. Row 4 is the scenario that files a hand-typed log task into the collection; row 5 the one that cancels a task because its eid is missing from the log. No scenario exercises rows 1, 3, 6, 7 or 8. A scenario with no row is not thereby one whose old answer this plugin keeps: several old answers are overturned by #709's own decisions 8 to 11 without a row of their own — a date moved later, a re-indent, a one-sided edit the old `direction` skipped — and #814 carries that list.

Content: every task, name, date and id is the old suite's own, and each was read before it was kept — all placeholders (`My Project`, `Write report`, `abc123` and the like). One change: the two IT-8 scenarios' log held the Swedish notes heading a real day's log carries, and now holds `# Notes`, in the texts and in one assertion's message; the old code treats any level-1 heading alike, and its output was recorded on the renamed text rather than edited afterwards. The four section headings are the old plugin's shipped defaults (`DEFAULT_SETTINGS` in its `src/types.ts`), not taken from any one day. The completed heading has to stay Swedish, because the old code finds it by a fixed pattern (`RE_SLUTFORD_HEADING`) whatever it is told; the other three reach the old code as settings and could have been renamed, and are kept so the four read as the old plugin's one default set.

source.repository: The pre-merge Effortless plugin's clone, ~/Devbox/Effortless, on the laptop only; never pushed.

reasons.breadcrumb: Asserts that the log line contains the literal `[[My Project]]`. The old plugin rebuilt that breadcrumb on every write; here the collection's name is ordinary visible text, written once at copy time and carried untouched after that, so its literal form is no longer an expectation.
reasons.rebuildShape: None dropped for this reason, and it is kept here so the count says so: no old assertion pins the shape of a rebuilt line — each reads a line with `includes`, a prefix or a position. The scenarios whose old output holds a rebuilt line carry named difference 2 instead.
